headline: Medium risk: dbt-core can write to warehouses while pdf.js parses PDFs, creating modest leakage and workflow-conflict risks; no direct prompt-injection channel is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented between dbt-core and pdf.js. dbt-core only calls data warehouse APIs, while pdf.js reads PDF files and runs browser-based tests; neither profile shows default ingestion of the other's outputs as instructions. Uncertainty is low enough to keep this at none.
conditions: IF a shared clipboard, MCP server, or filesystem bridge is added between dbt-core and pdf.js, reassess prompt-injection risk.
IF pdf.js output is manually copied into dbt-core command inputs, the pathway becomes user-mediated.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Avoid copy-pasting rendered PDF text into dbt-core prompts or configs.
Disable any shared clipboard or message bus between the two tools.

B_data_leakage.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data and has allowlisted network egress, while pdf.js touches PDF documents and has no network egress. If PDFs or warehouse exports are placed in a shared workspace, either agent could expose sensitive content through its normal processing path. The pairwise leakage pathway exists in default-ish workflows, so medium fits.
conditions: IF dbt-core and pdf.js share a filesystem or workspace containing sensitive PDFs or warehouse extracts, leakage risk is present.
IF dbt-core sends warehouse-derived artifacts to external services through its allowlisted egress, data exposure increases.
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct directories.
Store sensitive PDFs and warehouse exports in different access-controlled locations.
Review dbt-core egress allowlist before running on sensitive data.
Run pdf.js on redacted copies when possible.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: dbt-core has network egress to data warehouses, and pdf.js supports multiple instances with browser-based tests, but neither profile shows overlapping write access to the same mutable resource. Without a shared writable target, conflict is limited and mostly requires unusual orchestration.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same warehouse objects or shared files, write conflicts become plausible.
IF an orchestrator assigns both agents the same mutable resource without locking, contention can occur.
mitigations: Enable resource locking in the orchestrator.
Use read-only access for pdf.js where possible.

D_cascading_error.rationale: dbt-core can generate warehouse-facing transformations, and pdf.js can render or inspect PDFs, but neither profile proves that one agent automatically trusts the other's output. Still, if pdf.js-derived text is fed into dbt-core or dbt-core outputs are treated as authoritative without review, errors can cascade across work products. Uncertainty favors medium.
conditions: IF pdf.js extracted text is used as authoritative input to dbt-core transformations without verification, cascading error risk exists.
IF dbt-core outputs are rendered into PDFs and then reused as source-of-truth, downstream mistakes can propagate.
mitigations: Add a human verification step between agents.
Require schema or checksum validation on transferred artifacts.
Mark derived PDFs and warehouse outputs as non-authoritative until reviewed.
Keep provenance metadata with each handoff.

E_compliance.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data and can egress to allowlisted network destinations, while pdf.js processes PDF documents locally with no network egress. If regulated data is present, differing handling paths can create retention or residency mismatches. The profiles do not show a specific jurisdiction, so this is a general compliance gap rather than a confirmed breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the warehouse and also embedded in PDFs, retention or residency controls may diverge.
IF dbt-core egress is used on data subject to strict locality rules, compliance review is required.
mitigations: Confirm retention settings for both workflows.
Restrict dbt-core egress for regulated datasets.
Use redaction for PDFs containing sensitive fields.
